summary: Escape in a search field that is already empty gives the keyboard to the files. It was a dead key there. The Nushell filter's field does the same, and its bar stays open. With text in either field Escape does what it did: the kit empties the field, which ends the search at once and turns the filter off after its 400 ms pause, and the keyboard stays in the field. Two capture-phase listeners for the kit's input::Escape action, one on the search field's wrapper (src/finder/toolbar.rs, render_toolbar, beside the Down Arrow listener) and one on the filter bar's row (src/finder/filter.rs, render_filter_bar), call focus_files and stop the action when the field's value is empty; otherwise they leave it to the field. clean_on_escape stays on both fields and src/finder/mod.rs is untouched. docs/manual.md has a sentence in Searching, one in the filter paragraph, and an Escape row in the 'In the search field' table.
changelog: Escape in a search field that is already empty gives the keyboard back to the files, so the arrow keys, Space, and typing to select work again without a click. With words in the field, Escape still empties it and ends the search, and the keyboard stays in the field for other words. The Nushell filter's field does the same: Escape empties it, and in an empty field Escape gives the keyboard to the files and leaves the filter bar open. In a `--pick` chooser, where Escape in the files cancels, pressing Escape over and over in the search field now ends in Cancel. It used to stop at the empty field.
behaviour_changes: Escape in a search field that is already empty gives the keyboard to the files. It was a dead key. This also works in an empty folder, in each of the four views, and right after a Cmd+F pressed by mistake.
Escape in an already-empty Nushell filter field gives the keyboard to the files, and the filter bar stays open. It was a dead key.

Unchanged: with text in either field, Escape empties it and the keyboard stays in the field, so other words can be typed. The search ends at once. The filter turns off after its 400 ms pause, so two fast presses in the filter field leave for the files while the filter is still on for the rest of that pause (probed).

Consequence: after Escape, Escape the keys are the files'. Letters select by name (before, they started a new search or became a filter), and the arrow keys, Space (Quick Look), Return (open), Cmd+A, Delete (Move to Trash) and Cmd+Z (undo the latest file operation) act on the files, including on the selection the folder had before the search, which comes back when the search ends. The move shows: the field loses its ring, and in the list view the selection turns from grey to the active colour.

A third Escape, now in the files, does what Escape in the files always did: it cancels a cut, else clears the selection, else ends a search or cancels a chooser (probed with a cut pending: the third press lets go of the cut, the fourth clears the selection).

File chooser (`--pick`): repeated Escape from the search field now reaches Cancel and exit 1, and so does a held key. One press empties, one leaves, one clears the selection if one came back, the next cancels. Before, no number of presses in the field cancelled. One press from an empty field only moves the keyboard (probed: the chooser is still open after Cmd+F, Escape, and after three presses from a field with words and a selection).
Split view: the keyboard goes to the files of the pane whose field it was (probed in both panes, by key and by a click in the split pane's field; a letter then selected in that pane only).

If the keyboard came to the search field from the sidebar's folder tree, Escape in the empty field goes to the files, not back to the tree. This follows from the code (focus_files always names the files); I did not probe it.
Spaces-only text counts as text: the first Escape empties the field, the second leaves (probed in both fields).

The field's own right-click menu on Linux: Escape closes the menu and the keyboard is back in the still-empty field; the next Escape leaves (probed for both fields). On macOS and Windows that menu is native and the key does not reach the app.
After a dialog (Search Syntax, Cmd+/) or a toolbar menu opened over an empty search field is closed with Escape, the keyboard is back in the field, and the next Escape leaves for the files (probed).

Unchanged: Escape in the Nushell panel's field, in a name being edited, and in dialogs. The new listeners hear only their own field (probed: the panel's field keeps its text and the keyboard; a rename is cancelled as before with the search field empty and an empty filter bar open).
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.
The Nushell panel's field (nu_input): Escape there still does nothing. It is not in the brief. See Found, not fixed.

No committed test for the file chooser, split view, the right-click menu, dialogs, or spaces-only text. All were run as scratch tests in this review and deleted. The chooser's cancelling press cannot be tested at all: picker::cancel() exits the process. The right-click menu is native on macOS and Windows, so a test of it would not run there.

No test for an input method's composition; the harness cannot make one. Read instead: marked text is written into the buffer that value() returns and an empty preedit clears the mark (gpui-base input/base/state.rs, replace_and_mark_text_in_range); on macOS a key pressed while composing goes to the input method first and reaches the app only if the input method hands it back (gpui-pre-macos window.rs, is_composing); on X11 a dead-key sequence that Escape cancels is committed to the field before the key is dispatched, so the field is not empty. In each case Escape during a composition is left to the field, as before.

No guard against a held key. Key repeat reaches the app as presses, an action listener is not told that a key is held, and on macOS gpui reports is_held as false for keys that come back through doCommandBySelector. So holding Escape in a field with text empties it, leaves it, and goes on to Escape in the files.
Nothing was run on macOS or Windows. The change adds no cfg-specific code and no imports: the action is named by its full path, as toolbar.rs already names the kit's Undo and Redo.
`cargo clippy --features term` was not run: src/term is untouched and no signature changed.

README.md and the Search Syntax dialog needed no change; neither mentions Escape in a field. The manual's chooser section still says only 'Escape or Cancel exits 1'; the field's Escape is in the 'In the search field' table.
tests: tests/controls.rs: escape_in_an_empty_search_field_gives_the_files_the_keyboard (after search_field_typing_escape_and_down_arrow, which is untouched). Fails without the change at 'the second Escape leaves the field'. It also pins Escape-then-retype, a letter going to the files afterwards, and the empty folder.

tests/controls.rs: escape_in_an_empty_filter_field_gives_the_files_the_keyboard (after the_keys_on_the_filter_bars_close_button_remove_the_filter). Fails without the change at 'the second Escape leaves the field'. It also pins that the first Escape stays in the field and that the bar stays open.
review_fixes: Commit message: the Changelog entry now says what changes in a `--pick` chooser (Escape pressed over and over in the search field ends in Cancel). It is the one place where this change can end a session, and the entry is what users will read. The body's sentence on the chooser said one press always goes to a selection; it now says 'if one came back'.
tests/controls.rs: a comment in the new search test read 'A letter selects an item now', which can be taken for a note about the change. It now says where the keyboard is.
No change to the code or the manual. I found nothing wrong in them.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit: 526 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The trunk had not moved since the lane's base (82f79a2), so the rebase was a no-op. Pushed to origin (82f79a2..9cf7635). The implementer's commit was 8501be9; the trunk commit differs from it by one test comment and the message.

How it was checked. With the src diff reverse-applied, both new tests fail at 'the second Escape leaves the field'; with it back they pass, in 25 runs under SEED 1 to 25. Scratch tests, deleted afterwards, covered what the committed tests leave out: a chooser (alive after one press from an empty field, and after three from a field with words and a selection), split view (both panes), the Nushell panel's field and a rename (both untouched), the right-click menus of both fields, a dialog and a toolbar menu over an empty search field, a cut, the four views, spaces-only text, two fast presses in the filter field, and Return then two fast presses while a search has yet to answer (the keyboard ends in the files with nothing selected and the folder showing). I took seven pictures of my own (list view light, filter bar dark, icon view) and compared them with the implementer's nine, which are the ones kept.

Why each listener hears only its own field. Every element gets a dispatch node of its own (gpui-pre element.rs: prepaint pushes one), so a capture listener on the wrapper or on the bar's row sees only actions sent from inside it, and only a kit input sends input::Escape (it is bound in the Input context). While a menu or a dialog has the keyboard, the key is found in that menu's or dialog's own context and goes no further. For an empty single-line field the kit's own Escape handler does nothing that losing the keyboard doesn't also do (the completion hooks are no-ops outside the code editor, and on_blur also dismisses a touch selection), so nothing is skipped by stopping the action ahead of it.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code says.
1. A chooser ended by accident. Escape in the files cancels a chooser (Finder::escape, mod.rs) and the keyboard now gets there from the search field. It takes a press that happens in the files, after the field is empty and left; the capture stops the action, and no other binding for Escape matches in the field, so one press never does two things. A held key does run through all of them. This matches the manual's 'Escape or Cancel exits 1' and what a native open panel does, and the Changelog entry now says it.
2. Keys meant for the field acting on files. After the second Escape, letters select, Space opens Quick Look, Return opens, Delete trashes the selection that came back with the folder, and Cmd+Z undoes a file operation where in the field it was the field's own Undo. These are the files' ordinary keys, the first Escape still stays in the field (pinned by the test's retype), and the move shows in the field's ring and the selection's colour. This is the behaviour the brief asks for.
3. The keyboard going to the wrong place or nowhere. focus_files focuses the files of the browser whose toolbar or filter bar it is, and the file area is always drawn (render_content), so there is nothing to lose it to. An empty field means no search is on, because every place that sets the query also sets the field (Finder::new, open_request, open_smart_folder, end_search), so there is nothing left to end.

For briefs still to come.
- recent-searches: the search field's wrapper in toolbar.rs now has a capture_action for the kit's input::Escape beside the capture_key_down you have to guard. It looks at the field's value, not at which element inside the wrapper has the keyboard. With your menu open the key is the menu's (its Cancel is found first and PopupMenu::dismiss does not pass it on), but pin it: open the menu over an empty field, press Escape, and assert the menu is closed and the files do not have the keyboard. If you write the focus guard for Down as a helper, put this capture behind it too. Escape in an empty field now leaves it, so the original test plan's 'Cmd+F, Escape, Up' sends Up to the files; the verifier's step 8 (Cmd+F, Up) is unaffected, and so are 'type atlas, press escape' (stays in the field) and step 1's two presses after Return (they happen in the files). The Searching paragraph and the 'In the search field' table each gained a line here; the Escape row is the table's last.
- back-forward-restore-search: restore_search must set the field's value together with the query, as your plan says. Escape in the field takes an empty field to mean there is no search to end, and moves to the files without ending one.
- smart-folder-save-and-leaks: Escape with words in the search field still goes through the kit's clean(), which emits Change and so runs set_query(""). Escape in an empty field no longer reaches the field and emits nothing, as there is nothing to change. In the filter field Escape empties the field, Change runs set_filter("") after 400 ms, and the bar stays open because filter_open stays true.
- inactive-selection-colour: this change leans on the selection's colour to show where the keyboard went. In icon view the selection is drawn active while the keyboard is still in the search field (I took a picture of it), so there the only sign of the second Escape is the ring leaving the field, until your brief lands.
- split-active-pane: Escape in an empty search or filter field gives the keyboard to that pane's files, and Window::focus refreshes, so a contains_focused sync in Workspace::render sees it.
- focus-lost-recovery: independent. Two new callers of focus_files, both in key dispatch, where Window::focus redraws. An open, empty filter bar can now have the keyboard in the files by keys alone, not only after a click.
- search-syntax-click-example: when the dialog closes over an empty search field the keyboard is back in the field, and one more Escape leaves for the files.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change).
- The Nushell panel's field has no Escape of its own: the key does nothing there, with text or without (probed). It could take the same listener if the three fields should agree.
- With the filter bar open and the keyboard in the files, Cmd+Alt+F removes the filter and closes the bar; it never goes back to the field. So after Escape, Escape in the filter field the way back by keys is Cmd+Alt+F twice. Nothing is lost by it, since the field is empty by then. The same was true after a click on a file.
- A selection is lost when a filter hides its item and does not come back when the filter is emptied, unlike a search, which brings the folder's selection back when it ends (seen in my filter pictures).
- The UI tests' hang watchdog (tests/common/mod.rs, active_steps) is started from the first test thread that takes a step, so its thread inherits libtest's output capture, and process::exit(101) ends the run before the captured line is printed. A hang then shows as cargo's 'error: test failed' with no test lines and no reason. The implementer saw exactly that once, under load right after a restart. I did not reproduce it (it needs a step longer than 20 s); it is read from the code.
